pw.footer: sealed on your device with a passphrase of its own · on every device you sign in on · nothing readable on the relays
pw.empty: The vault is empty. Add a login with the round button, or bring your passwords from another manager in the settings.
pw.entryGone: This entry is no longer in the vault.

pw.unreadable.one: {n} entry was sealed with a vault removed since and cannot be read.
pw.unreadable.other: {n} entries were sealed with a vault removed since and cannot be read.

pw.deleteText: It is gone from all your devices. Earlier backups still hold it.
pw.field.name: Name
pw.badSecret: That is neither a 2FA secret nor an otpauth:// link.
pw.how.generator: Made on your device from the browser’s secure random numbers. A passphrase’s words come from the BIP-39 list of 2048 words, so each adds 11 bits; six words are a good passphrase, twenty characters a good password.

pw.health.intro.one: {n} password looked at on this device.
pw.health.intro.other: {n} passwords looked at on this device.

pw.health.breachOff: The breach check is off: it asks an outside service.
pw.health.toSettings: Turn it on in the settings
pw.health.breachText: Have I Been Pwned is asked with the first five characters of each password’s hash only; the passwords never leave this device.
pw.health.noBreaches: None of your passwords is in a known breach.
pw.settings.breachOn: Check my passwords against known breaches
pw.settings.breachText: Off unless you turn it on. When you start a check in Health, Have I Been Pwned gets the first five characters of each password’s SHA-1 hash, nothing more, and answers with every hash that starts so; the match is found here.
pw.settings.importText: Import takes a vault backup (with its passphrase), a plain export of Bitwarden (JSON or CSV), KeePass (XML) or KeePassXC, the CSV of Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari, 1Password, LastPass, Dashlane or Proton Pass, or a list of otpauth:// links. What is already here is skipped.
pw.import.encrypted: This export is encrypted: export it from Bitwarden as plain JSON.
pw.how.1: Each entry is its own event on your relays, sealed with the vault’s key; relays see how many entries you have and when they change, nothing else.
pw.how.2: A web page cannot fill in other sites’ forms (that needs a browser extension): copy the username and password, or open the site from the entry.
